entities.name: Louis XIV of France
entities.label: Person
entities.summary:
Louis XIV (1638–1715), the 'Sun King,' was King of France for 72 years (1643–1715) — the longest verified reign of any sovereign in European history. His rule epitomized absolute monarchy: 'L'État, c'est moi' ('I am the state') captured his belief that royal authority was indivisible and divinely ordained.

He built the Palace of Versailles — transforming a hunting lodge into the most magnificent court in Europe, where 10,000 nobles competed for royal favor. French became the language of European diplomacy, French fashion set Continental trends, and French arts (Molière, Racine, Lully) defined the Baroque age.

Yet his ambitions overreached: the Revocation of the Edict of Nantes (1685) expelled 200,000 Huguenots, draining France of skilled workers. His wars of expansion — the War of Spanish Succession chief among them — exhausted the treasury. He left France culturally triumphant but financially ruined, sowing seeds for the Revolution 74 years later.
